bounds.domain: Two credential intent owners, one symbolic credential slot, three replacement values including removal, and one resident stop lease. Writer identities stand for distinct intent, lifecycle and stop counters. Each changed writer can reserve one unique stop lease. A launch retires the prior lease identity. Counters never wrap.
bounds.assumptions: All writers use the same lifecycle and vault locks. There is no out-of-band slot write or resident relaunch between the sampled process absence and the final commit. Actual stop request delivery and observed absence are separate. A changed write can return with an exact readback, with the value still missing, or with an effect whose readback failed. The unchanged fast path models its successful readback only.
bounds.limitations: The model covers one resident mutation protocol. It excludes persistence across process death, actual Android process inventory, failed reservation before a stop exists, native record removal failures, external vault writes, and arbitrary owners. The JVM compiles the exact intent fence, conductor, slot mutation, and lease and extracts the app lifecycle binding. The harness supplies only the resident process, clock, and vault boundaries.

assumptions: Weak fairness of each reserved writer's progress. It is eventually dispatched, and its retirement wait eventually receives enough replies or reaches its timeout. Storage work and cleanup return. This includes explicit failures.
No fairness assumes the stop is confirmed, a write succeeds, an unconfirmed lease is released, or another writer arrives.
No fairness. A reserved writer may remain queued, or a started retirement may never receive a reply or a deadline tick.
